blurb.en: Choose the right word for each sentence, then fill the gaps in short stories.
blurb.vi: Chọn từ đúng cho mỗi câu, rồi điền vào chỗ trống trong những câu chuyện ngắn.

title.vi: Từ chỉ thời gian và từ nối

countable.def: A noun you can count: one apple, two apples, three apples.
countable.ex: An egg is *countable*: one egg, two eggs.

uncountable.def: A noun you cannot count, like water, rice or sugar. It has no plural.
uncountable.ex: Rice is *uncountable*. We say 'some rice', not 'two rices'.

a few.vi: một vài (dùng với danh từ đếm được)
a few.def: A small number of things you can count.
a few.ex: There are *a few* grapes left in the bowl.

a little.vi: một chút, một ít (dùng với danh từ không đếm được)
a little.def: A small amount of something you cannot count.
a little.ex: Put *a little* honey on your bread.

nothing.def: Not one thing. It means the same as 'not anything'.
nothing.ex: The box was empty. There was *nothing* in it.

connective.def: A joining word, like when, then or while, that links two ideas.
connective.ex: 'When' is a *connective* in 'When it rained, we went inside.'

before.ex: Brush your teeth *before* you go to bed.

already.def: Sooner than you thought, or at some time before now.

yet.vi: chưa (cuối câu phủ định và câu hỏi)
yet.def: Up to now. It goes at the end of 'not' sentences and questions.

gap.def: An empty space in a sentence where a word is missing.
gap.ex: Read the whole sentence, then choose a word for the *gap*.

clue.def: A small piece of information that helps you find the answer.
clue.ex: 'Yesterday' is a *clue*: the verb must be in the past.

tag question.def: A short question at the end of a sentence, like 'isn't it?' or 'do you?'
tag question.ex: 'It's hot, isn't it?' ends with a *tag question*.

verb pattern.vi: mẫu động từ (to + động từ hoặc động từ + -ing)
verb pattern.def: The form of the next verb: to + verb, or verb + -ing.
verb pattern.ex: 'enjoy + -ing' is a *verb pattern*: I enjoy swimming.

title.en: A few, a little, some, any
title.vi: A few, a little, some, any

scenes.head: A note from Dad on the fridge
scenes.html:
Finn,
Please go to the shop with Grandpa after school. We need *a few* eggs and *a little* sugar for the cake. Please buy *some* oranges too. We have *nothing* in the fruit bowl! We don't need *any* rice: there is *a lot of* rice in the cupboard.
Thanks!
Dad

steps.en: *a few* goes with things you can count, like eggs. *a little* goes with things you can't count, like sugar.
steps.vi: *a few* đi với những thứ đếm được, như trứng. *a little* đi với những thứ không đếm được, như đường.

steps.en: Use *some* in positive sentences. Use *any* in 'not' sentences and in questions.
steps.vi: Dùng *some* trong câu khẳng định. Dùng *any* trong câu phủ định và câu hỏi.

steps.en: *nothing* means 'not anything'. 'We have nothing' = 'We don't have anything'.
steps.vi: *nothing* nghĩa là 'không có gì'. 'We have nothing' = 'We don't have anything'.

title.en: Already, yet, might, have to and tags
title.vi: Already, yet, might, have to và câu hỏi đuôi

scenes.head: A chat in the playground
scenes.html:
Ivy: Have you finished your planet poster *yet*?
Finn: Yes, I've *already* finished it. I *enjoy drawing* planets!
Ivy: Your poster is really good, *isn't it*? I haven't started mine *yet*.
Finn: You *might* need some help. I can help you *after* school.
Ivy: Thanks! I *have to* give it to the teacher on Friday.

steps.en: *already* goes in positive sentences. *yet* goes at the end of questions and 'not' sentences.
steps.vi: *already* dùng trong câu khẳng định. *yet* đứng cuối câu hỏi và câu phủ định.

steps.en: *isn't it?* is a tag question. A positive sentence (is) gets a negative tag (isn't).
steps.vi: *isn't it?* là câu hỏi đuôi. Câu khẳng định (is) đi với đuôi phủ định (isn't).
*might* = có thể, có lẽ. *have to* = phải, cần thiết.

steps.en: After *enjoy*, the next verb ends in -ing: *enjoy drawing*.
steps.vi: Sau *enjoy*, động từ tiếp theo thêm -ing: *enjoy drawing*.

title.vi: Đọc một bài kể chuyện ngắn

scenes.head: A recount by Ivy
scenes.html:
Our Walk up the Hill
Last Monday, our class walked up a small hill *to look* at the clouds. The path was wet, so we walked *more carefully* than usual. *Each* child had a notebook. *When* we got to the top, we drew the clouds. *Then* it started to rain, and we ran back down. Finn ran *faster* than everyone!

steps.en: In a story with gaps, read the sentence before and the sentence after the gap.
steps.vi: Trong bài có chỗ trống, hãy đọc câu đứng trước và câu đứng sau chỗ trống.

steps.en: *to look* tells us WHY the class went: to + verb gives a reason.
steps.vi: *to look* cho biết VÌ SAO cả lớp đi: to + động từ chỉ mục đích.

steps.en: *more carefully* and *faster* compare how people do things. Look for 'than'.
steps.vi: *more carefully* và *faster* so sánh cách mọi người làm việc. Hãy tìm từ 'than'.

end.en: Great work! You chose the right grammar words.
end.vi: Làm tốt lắm! Em đã chọn đúng các từ ngữ pháp.

challenge.result: You spotted amounts, time words, tags and verb patterns!

v.q: Can I have ________ juice, please?
whys: 'a few' goes with things you can count. Can you count juice?
'many' goes with plural nouns you can count, like 'many cups'.
v.hint: Can you count juice? Choose the word for things you can't count.
v.worked: Juice is uncountable, so we say *a little* juice.

v.q: There are ________ birds in the tree.
whys: 'a little' goes with things you can't count. Birds are easy to count.
'much' goes with things you can't count, like 'much water'.
v.hint: Look at 'birds'. Is it a plural noun you can count?
v.worked: Birds can be counted, so we say *a few* birds.

v.q: I have ________ cleaned my room. Look!
whys: 'yet' goes at the end of questions and 'not' sentences.
'ever' is for questions like 'Have you ever ...?'
v.hint: Is this a positive sentence, a 'not' sentence or a question?
v.worked: In a positive sentence we say *have already cleaned*.

v.q: Finn hasn't finished his poster ________.
whys: 'already' goes in positive sentences, not after 'hasn't'.
'ever' doesn't go at the end of a 'not' sentence like this.
v.hint: Find 'hasn't'. Which word goes at the end of a 'not' sentence?
v.worked: 'hasn't finished' is negative, so it ends with *yet*.

v.q: This cake is delicious, ________?
whys: The sentence is positive (is), so the tag must be negative.
The verb is 'is', so the tag uses 'is', not 'does'.
v.hint: Find the verb in the sentence. Is the sentence positive or negative?
v.worked: 'This cake *is* delicious' is positive, so the tag is *isn't it*?

v.q: You can't swim, ________?
whys: The sentence is negative (can't), so the tag must be positive.
The verb is 'can', so the tag uses 'can', not 'do'.
v.hint: Find the verb. Is it positive or negative? Use the opposite in the tag.
v.worked: 'You *can't* swim' is negative, so the tag is *can you*?

v.q: We went up the hill ________ look at the clouds.
whys: We don't say 'for look'. Use to + verb for a reason.
'because' needs a full sentence after it, like 'because we wanted ...'.
v.hint: The gap tells us WHY they went. Which word goes before a verb to give a reason?
v.worked: To give a reason with a verb, we use *to* + verb: *to look*.

v.q: Finn walks ________ than his little brother.
whys: 'fast' doesn't compare. With 'than' we need the comparative.
'fastest' is for the top one of a group, not with 'than'.
v.hint: Look for 'than'. It needs a comparing word.
v.worked: With *than* we use the comparative: *faster* than.

title.en: Amounts: a few, a little, some, any
title.vi: Số lượng: a few, a little, some, any

v.q: There are only ________ grapes left in the bowl.
whys: 'a little' is for things you can't count, like milk. Grapes are easy to count.
'much' is for things you can't count, like 'much rice'.
v.hint: Look at 'grapes'. Can you count them?
v.worked: Grapes are countable and plural, so we say *a few* grapes.

v.q: We need ________ flour to make the bread.
whys: 'a few' is for things you can count. Can you count flour?
'many' is for plural nouns you can count, like 'many eggs'.
v.hint: Can you count flour? Choose the word for things you can't count.
v.worked: Flour is uncountable, so we say *a little* flour.

v.q: There isn't ________ water in the bottle.
whys: 'some' is for positive sentences. This sentence has 'isn't'.
'isn't' and 'nothing' are both negative. We don't use two negatives.
v.hint: Find 'isn't'. Which word goes in a 'not' sentence?
v.worked: In a 'not' sentence we use *any*: there *isn't any* water.

v.q: I'm hungry. I want ________ to eat.
whys: 'anything' is for questions and 'not' sentences. 'I want' is positive.
A hungry person wants food, so 'nothing' doesn't make sense.
v.hint: Is the sentence positive or negative? Then think about the meaning.
v.worked: 'I want' is positive and the person is hungry: *something* to eat.

v.q: Write some, any or nothing.
lines: We haven't got {0} bread. Can you buy some?
v.hint: Find 'haven't'. Which of the three words goes in a 'not' sentence?
v.worked: 'haven't got' is negative, so we write *any*.

v.q: Write some, any or nothing.
lines: The box is empty. There is {0} in it.
v.hint: The box is empty. Which word means 'not anything'?
v.worked: The box is empty, so there is *nothing* in it.

title.en: Have to, might, already, yet, tags
title.vi: Have to, might, already, yet, câu hỏi đuôi

v.q: Take your umbrella. It ________ rain later.
whys: Rain is not a rule. We can't say the rain has to come.
'later' is in the future, so 'had to' (past) is wrong.
v.hint: Is this a rule, or something that will maybe happen?
v.worked: We are not sure it will rain, so we say it *might* rain.

v.q: At our school, we ________ wear a uniform every day.
whys: A uniform is a school rule, not a 'maybe'.
'every day' is about now, so 'had to' (past) is wrong.
v.hint: Is this a rule or a 'maybe'? Is it now or in the past?
v.worked: It is a school rule, every day: we *have to* wear a uniform.

v.q: Look! I've ________ made my bed.
whys: 'yet' goes at the end of questions and 'not' sentences.
'ever' is for questions like 'Have you ever ...?'
v.hint: Is the sentence positive, negative or a question?
v.worked: It is positive and the bed is done: I've *already* made my bed.

v.q: Dad hasn't come home ________.
whys: 'already' goes in positive sentences, not after 'hasn't'.
'ever' doesn't go at the end of a 'not' sentence like this.
v.hint: Find 'hasn't'. Which word goes at the end of a 'not' sentence?
v.worked: 'hasn't come' is negative, so we finish with *yet*.

v.q: Zac likes rice, ________?
whys: The verb is 'likes', so the tag uses 'does', not 'is'.
The sentence is positive, so the tag must be negative.
v.hint: 'likes' has no helping verb. Which helping verb goes with it?
v.worked: 'Zac *likes*' is present simple and positive: *doesn't he*?

v.q: Molly isn't at home, ________?
whys: The sentence is already negative (isn't), so the tag is positive.
The verb is 'is', so the tag uses 'is', not 'does'.
v.hint: Find the verb. Is it positive or negative? Use the opposite in the tag.
v.worked: 'Molly *isn't*' is negative, so the tag is *is she*?

title.vi: Từ nối và mẫu động từ

v.q: Turn off the lights ________ you leave the room.
whys: 'then' starts a new step. It can't join 'Turn off the lights' and 'you leave'.
'while' is for two long things at the same time, not leaving a room.
v.hint: Which word joins the two parts and tells us the time?
v.worked: Turn off the lights at the time you leave: *when* you leave the room.

v.q: Mum cooked dinner. ________ we all ate together.
whys: 'While we all ate together' is not a full sentence on its own.
'Before we all ate together' is not a full sentence on its own.
v.hint: There are two sentences. Which word starts the next step?
v.worked: First Mum cooked. *Then* we ate: *Then* starts the next step.

v.q: Write the verb in brackets in the right form.
v.hint: What form of the verb comes after 'enjoy'?
v.worked: After *enjoy* we use verb + -ing: *swimming*.

v.q: Write the verb in brackets in the right form.
lines: Zac finished {0} (read) his book at nine o'clock.
v.hint: What form of the verb comes after 'finish'?
v.worked: After *finished* we use verb + -ing: *reading*.

v.q: Ivy sings ________ than her brother.
whys: 'good' doesn't compare, and 'than' needs a comparing word.
'best' is for the top one of a group, not with 'than'.
v.hint: Look for 'than'. Which word compares two people?
v.worked: well, *better*, best: with *than* we say *better*.

v.q: Finn writes ________ than me. His letters are very neat.
whys: 'most carefully' is for the top one of a group, not with 'than'.
'carefully' doesn't compare. With 'than' we need 'more'.
v.hint: Look for 'than'. Long adverbs use 'more' to compare.
v.worked: With *than* and a long adverb we use *more carefully*.

blurb.en: Practise Reading Part 3 (circle the word) and Part 4 (a story with seven gaps).
blurb.vi: Luyện Phần 3 của bài Đọc (khoanh từ đúng) và Phần 4 (câu chuyện có bảy chỗ trống).

v.q: Your sister can ride a bike, ________?
whys: The sentence is positive (can), so the tag must be negative.
The verb is 'can', so the tag uses 'can', not 'does'.
v.hint: Find the verb. Use the same verb in the tag, but the opposite (positive or negative).
v.worked: 'can ride' is positive, so the tag is *can't she*?

v.q: They don't live near the park, ________?
whys: The sentence is negative (don't), so the tag must be positive.
The sentence uses 'do', so the tag uses 'do', not 'are'.
v.hint: Find the helping verb. Is it positive or negative?
v.worked: 'They *don't* live' is negative, so the tag is *do they*?

v.q: Can I have ________ water, please? I'm thirsty.
whys: 'a few' is for things you can count. Can you count water?
'many' is for plural nouns you can count, like 'many glasses'.
v.hint: Can you count water? Choose the word for things you can't count.
v.worked: Water is uncountable, so we say *a little* water.

v.q: There isn't ________ cheese in the fridge.
whys: 'many' is for plural nouns you can count. Cheese is uncountable here.
'a few' is for things you can count, like 'a few eggs'.
v.hint: Is 'cheese' countable or uncountable here?
v.worked: Cheese is uncountable, so we say *isn't much* cheese.

v.q: There isn't ________ in my school bag.
whys: 'something' is for positive sentences. This sentence has 'isn't'.
'isn't' and 'nothing' are both negative. We don't use two negatives.
v.hint: Find 'isn't'. Which word goes in a 'not' sentence?
v.worked: In a 'not' sentence we use *anything*: there *isn't anything*.

v.q: Look! There's ________ under the table. What is it?
whys: 'anything' is for questions and 'not' sentences. 'There's' is positive.
The child asks 'What is it?', so there must be a thing there.
v.hint: Is the sentence positive? Then read the question after it.
v.worked: 'There's' is positive and the child asks 'What is it?': *something*.

v.q: Put on your coat ________ you go outside.
whys: You need your coat outside, so you can't put it on later.
'while you go outside' doesn't make sense: you put a coat on first.
v.hint: Think about the order. Which happens first?
v.worked: First the coat, then outside: put on your coat *before* you go outside.

v.q: Wash the cups, ________ put them on the shelf.
whys: 'before put' is wrong. After 'before' we need 'you put'.
'while put' is wrong. After 'while' we need 'you put'.
v.hint: These are two instructions. Which word starts the next step?
v.worked: Wash the cups, *then* put them on the shelf: *then* starts the next step.

v.q: My brother loves ________ football with his friends.
whys: After 'loves' we don't use the base form 'play'.
'loves' is the verb already. We can't add 'plays' after it.
v.hint: What form of the verb comes after 'love'?
v.worked: love + -ing: loves *playing* football.

v.q: We would like ________ the new museum next week.
whys: After 'would like' we don't use -ing.
After 'would like' we need 'to' before the verb.
v.hint: What comes after 'would like': to + verb or verb + -ing?
v.worked: would like + to + verb: *to visit*.

title.en: Part 4: a story with gaps (gaps 1 to 4)
title.vi: Phần 4: câu chuyện có chỗ trống (chỗ trống 1 đến 4)

v.q: Read the story. Gap (1): choose the word.
whys: After 'wanted' we don't use -ing.
After 'wanted' we need 'to' before the verb.
v.hint: Look at the word just before the gap. What comes after 'want'?
v.worked: want + to + verb: we wanted *to raise* money.

stim.head: A recount by Yen
stim.html:
Our Craft Stall
Last Saturday, there was a fun day for everyone in our neighbourhood. There were (0) many stalls at the sports club. Our class had a craft stall. We wanted (1) ________ money for the animal home near our school.
On Friday, we made paper flowers and bookmarks. My friend Zac paints (2) ________ than me, so he painted all the flowers. We needed lots of glue, but we didn't have (3) ________ glue in the classroom. Our teacher brought a big bottle from home.
On Saturday morning, there were grey clouds in the sky. Our teacher said, "It (4) ________ rain later. Let's put the stall under the trees."
(5) ________ we put out the flowers, people started to buy them. A lady picked up a flower and smiled at Zac. "You made these, (6) ________?" she said. Zac was very proud.
The fun day ended at five o'clock, but at three o'clock our teacher looked at the empty table and laughed. "We have (7) ________ sold everything!" she said. Now the animal home can buy food for its dogs and cats.

v.q: Read the story. Gap (1): choose the word.
whys: We don't say 'for learn'. Use to + verb for a reason.
'so' needs a full sentence after it, like 'so we could learn'.
v.hint: The gap tells us WHY they went. Which word goes before a verb to give a reason?
v.worked: They went there for a reason: *to* learn about the weather.

stim.head: A recount by Hamid
stim.html:
Our Trip to the Weather Station
Last Tuesday, our class went to a weather station on a hill. (0) Every child took a notebook and a pencil. We went there (1) ________ learn about the weather.
The road up the hill was very narrow, so our bus went slowly. A man on a bike went (2) ________ than our bus!
At the top, there were only (3) ________ people: a guide and two scientists. The guide said, "The wind is very strong today. You (4) ________ stay with your group."
First, we looked at a machine that measures the wind. (5) ________ we went outside to see a weather balloon. My friend Bella was shaking. "It's really cold up here, (6) ________?" she said. The guide smiled and gave her a hat.
The guide let the balloon go. It flew up into the grey sky and got smaller and smaller. I really enjoyed (7) ________ it fly away.
On the bus home, Bella and I talked about the balloon all the way. Now I want to be a scientist one day!

v.q: Read the story. Gap (2): choose the word.
whys: 'carefully' doesn't compare. Look at 'than me'.
'most carefully' is for the top one of a group, not with 'than'.
v.hint: Find the word after the gap. It tells you to compare two people.
v.worked: 'Zac paints ... *than* me': comparative, *more carefully*.

v.worked: 'went ... *than* our bus': comparative, *faster*.

Last Saturday, there was a fun day for everyone in our neighbourhood. There were (0) many stalls at the sports club. Our class had a craft stall. We wanted (1) ________ money for the animal home near our school.
On Friday, we made paper flowers and bookmarks. My friend Zac paints (2) ________ than me, so he painted all the flowers. We needed lots of glue, but we didn't have (3) ________ glue in the classroom. Our teacher brought a big bottle from home.
On Saturday morning, there were grey clouds in the sky. Our teacher said, "It (4) ________ rain later. Let's put the stall under the trees."
(5) ________ we put out the flowers, people started to buy them. A lady picked up a flower and smiled at Zac. "You made these, (6) ________?" she said. Zac was very proud.
The fun day ended at five o'clock, but at three o'clock our teacher looked at the empty table and laughed. "We have (7) ________ sold everything!" she said. Now the animal home can buy food for its dogs and cats.

items.en: Use *a few* and *many* with things you can count. Use *a little* and *much* with things you can't count. *each* and *every* go with one thing.
items.vi: Dùng *a few* và *many* với danh từ đếm được. Dùng *a little* và *much* với danh từ không đếm được. *each* và *every* đi với danh từ số ít.
example: There are *a few* eggs, but there isn't *much* milk.

items.en: Use *some* and *something* in positive sentences. Use *any* and *anything* in 'not' sentences and questions. *nothing* = not anything.
items.vi: Dùng *some* và *something* trong câu khẳng định. Dùng *any* và *anything* trong câu phủ định và câu hỏi. *nothing* = không có gì.
example: I've got *some* crayons, but I haven't got *any* paper.

items.en: Linking words show the order: *before*, *after*, *when*, *then*, *while*. Read the sentence before and after the gap.
items.vi: Từ nối cho biết thứ tự: *before*, *after*, *when*, *then*, *while*. Hãy đọc câu đứng trước và sau chỗ trống.
example: Put on your shoes *before* you go out.
*When* the bell rang, we went inside.

items.en: Use *to* + verb to say why. After *want*, *would like* and *hope* use *to* + verb. After *enjoy*, *love* and *finish* use verb + -ing.
items.vi: Dùng *to* + động từ để nói lí do, mục đích. Sau *want*, *would like*, *hope* dùng *to* + động từ. Sau *enjoy*, *love*, *finish* dùng động từ + -ing.
example: I went to the shop *to buy* bread.
I *want to learn* karate. I *enjoy swimming*.

items.en: *have to* = it is necessary (past: *had to*). *might* = maybe. *already* in positive sentences; *yet* at the end of questions and 'not' sentences.
items.vi: *have to* = phải, cần thiết (quá khứ: *had to*). *might* = có thể, có lẽ. *already* dùng trong câu khẳng định; *yet* đứng cuối câu hỏi và câu phủ định.
example: We *have to* wear a hat. It *might* be sunny.
I've *already* eaten, but Zac hasn't eaten *yet*.

items.en: Tag questions: positive sentence, negative tag; negative sentence, positive tag. To compare how people do things, use *faster*, *better*, *more carefully* + *than*.
items.vi: Câu hỏi đuôi: câu khẳng định đi với đuôi phủ định; câu phủ định đi với đuôi khẳng định. Để so sánh cách làm việc, dùng *faster*, *better*, *more carefully* + *than*.
example: It's windy, *isn't it*? You don't like fish, *do you*?
Ivy runs *faster than* me. She writes *more carefully than* me.

check.sentence: There are {a few|a little|much} oranges on the table.
Eat your breakfast {before|then|while} you go to school.
Mum went to the market {to buy|buying|buy} some fish.
Bella can swim, {can't she|can she|doesn't she}?

v.q: Hamid is in your class, ________?
whys: The sentence is positive (is), so the tag must be negative.
The verb is 'is', so the tag uses 'is', not 'does'.
v.hint: Find the verb. Use the same verb in the tag, but the opposite.
v.worked: 'Hamid *is*' is positive, so the tag is *isn't he*?

v.q: You've got a new bike, ________?
whys: 'You've got' is positive, so the tag must be negative.
'You've' means 'You have', so the tag uses 'have', not 'are'.
v.hint: What does 'You've' mean? Use that verb in the tag.
v.worked: 'You've (You *have*) got' is positive: *haven't you*?

v.q: Molly didn't come to school today, ________?
whys: The sentence is negative (didn't), so the tag must be positive.
The sentence uses 'did', so the tag uses 'did', not 'was'.
v.hint: Find the helping verb. Is it positive or negative?
v.worked: 'Molly *didn't* come' is negative: *did she*?

v.q: It isn't very cold today, ________?
whys: The sentence is negative (isn't), so the tag must be positive.
The verb is 'is', so the tag uses 'is', not 'does'.
v.hint: Find the verb. Is it positive or negative? Use the opposite in the tag.
v.worked: 'It *isn't*' is negative, so the tag is *is it*?

v.q: Please put ________ honey on my toast. Just one spoon.
whys: 'a few' is for things you can count. Can you count honey?
'many' is for plural nouns you can count, like 'many spoons'.
v.hint: Can you count honey? Choose the word for things you can't count.
v.worked: Honey is uncountable, so we say *a little* honey.

v.q: Ana has got ________ friends in her new class.
whys: 'a little' is for things you can't count. Friends are easy to count.
'much' is for things you can't count, like 'much time'.
v.hint: Look at 'friends'. Can you count them?
v.worked: Friends are countable and plural: *a few* friends.

v.q: We haven't got ________ eggs, so we can't make a cake.
whys: 'some' is for positive sentences. This sentence has 'haven't'.
'haven't' and 'nothing' are both negative. We don't use two negatives.
v.hint: Find 'haven't'. Which word goes in a 'not' sentence?
v.worked: In a 'not' sentence we use *any*: we *haven't got any* eggs.

v.q: Finn was bored. There was ________ to do at home.
whys: 'anything' is for questions and 'not' sentences. 'There was' is positive.
Finn was bored, so there was not one thing to do.
v.hint: Is 'There was' positive or negative? Then think: why was Finn bored?
v.worked: 'There was' is positive, and Finn was bored: *nothing* to do.

v.q: Dad went to the bank ________ get some money.
whys: We don't say 'for get'. Use to + verb for a reason.
'because' needs a full sentence after it, like 'because he needed money'.
v.hint: The gap tells us WHY Dad went. Which word goes before a verb to give a reason?
v.worked: To give a reason with a verb we use *to*: *to get* some money.

v.q: Grandma uses a big pot ________ cook rice.
whys: We don't say 'for cook'. Use to + verb for what something is used for.
'and' doesn't tell us what the pot is for, and 'Grandma ... and cook' is wrong.
v.hint: The gap tells us what the pot is FOR. Which word goes before the verb?
v.worked: To say what something is used for: a big pot *to* cook rice.

v.q: Read the story. Gap (1): choose the word.
whys: Read on: Phuc's dad had to bring more sticks, so they didn't have lots.
'a little' is for things you can't count. Sticks are easy to count.
v.hint: Read the sentence after the gap. Did the group have enough sticks?
v.worked: 'we *only* had ... Phuc's dad *brought more*': they had *a few* sticks.

stim.head: A recount by Molly
stim.html:
Our Model Homes
Last month, our class learned about homes around the world. (0) Each group made a model home. My group made a stilt house. I worked with Phuc and two other friends.
We needed lots of sticks for the tall posts, but we only had (1) ________ sticks. Phuc's dad brought more from his garden.
We glued the posts to a big piece of card. We (2) ________ wait for the glue to dry, so we couldn't paint the house until Friday.
(3) ________ the glue was dry, we painted the walls brown. Phuc looked in the craft box for some paper for the roof, but there was (4) ________ in it. So we used dry leaves from the playground.
Our group worked (5) ________ than the other groups, so we finished first. Our teacher looked at our house and said, "This house looks very strong, (6) ________?" We all smiled.
We have (7) ________ put our stilt house in the school hall. Come and see it!

v.q: Read the story. Gap (1): choose the word.
whys: Read on: they went in two groups, so there was not lots of space.
'a few' is for things you can count. Space is uncountable.
v.hint: Read the whole sentence. Why did they go in two groups?
v.worked: 'The kitchen is *very small*' and 'only': there was *a little* space.

stim.head: A recount by Long
stim.html:
Our Visit to the Bakery
Last Thursday, our class visited a small bakery near our school. There were (0) a lot of warm loaves on the shelves.
The kitchen is very small. There is only (1) ________ space in it, so we went in two groups.
The baker told us about his day. He (2) ________ get up at four o'clock every morning because people want fresh bread for breakfast.
Then he gave each of us some dough. (3) ________ we made our bread rolls, he showed us how to do it. My friend Ana wanted some chocolate for her roll, but there was (4) ________ in the kitchen. So she put sugar on it.
Ana's roll looked like a star, but mine looked like a potato! She worked (5) ________ than me.
Back at school, I asked, "Can we eat our rolls now?" Our teacher said, "They aren't cool (6) ________." So we waited ten minutes.
I enjoyed every minute of our visit. I'd like (7) ________ a baker one day!

v.q: Read the story. Gap (2): choose the word.
whys: 'so we couldn't paint' tells us they really waited. It wasn't a 'maybe'.
'couldn't' and 'until Friday' tell us the story is in the past.
v.hint: Read the rest of the sentence. Is it past or present? Was waiting necessary?
v.worked: Waiting was necessary ('*so we couldn't paint*'), in the past: *had to*.

We needed lots of sticks for the tall posts, but we only had (1) ________ sticks. Phuc's dad brought more from his garden.
We glued the posts to a big piece of card. We (2) ________ wait for the glue to dry, so we couldn't paint the house until Friday.
(3) ________ the glue was dry, we painted the walls brown. Phuc looked in the craft box for some paper for the roof, but there was (4) ________ in it. So we used dry leaves from the playground.
Our group worked (5) ________ than the other groups, so we finished first. Our teacher looked at our house and said, "This house looks very strong, (6) ________?" We all smiled.
We have (7) ________ put our stilt house in the school hall. Come and see it!

v.q: Read the story. Gap (5): choose the word.
whys: Ana's roll looked like a star, so she worked with more care, not less.
'most carefully' is for the top one of a group, not with 'than'.
v.hint: Read the sentence before. Whose roll looked better?
v.worked: Ana's roll looked like *a star* and mine like *a potato*: she worked *more carefully*.

Our Visit to the Bakery
Last Thursday, our class visited a small bakery near our school. There were (0) a lot of warm loaves on the shelves.
The kitchen is very small. There is only (1) ________ space in it, so we went in two groups.
The baker told us about his day. He (2) ________ get up at four o'clock every morning because people want fresh bread for breakfast.
Then he gave each of us some dough. (3) ________ we made our bread rolls, he showed us how to do it. My friend Ana wanted some chocolate for her roll, but there was (4) ________ in the kitchen. So she put sugar on it.
Ana's roll looked like a star, but mine looked like a potato! She worked (5) ________ than me.
Back at school, I asked, "Can we eat our rolls now?" Our teacher said, "They aren't cool (6) ________." So we waited ten minutes.
I enjoyed every minute of our visit. I'd like (7) ________ a baker one day!
